B02: LiveKit unit tests and behavior evaluation
B03: LiveKit Cloud deployment management and bounded rolling drain

replacement.title: Trace the voice pipeline
replacement.question: What happens from a spoken request to an audible answer?
answer: In this cascaded pipeline, published user audio reaches streaming STT, a selected turn policy chooses when to respond, the accepted input drives model generation, and TTS audio is published for browser playout. Several stages overlap. A realtime speech model combines different boundaries, so a diagram of sequential STT, LLM and TTS boxes cannot describe every deployment. If text-only realtime output is combined with separate TTS, verify that the selected provider supports that configuration rather than assuming model paths are interchangeable.

In the opt-in P2/joined path, durable admission precedes dispatched generation. Trace the original input and operation identity, the response generation, publication and observed playout separately. Text completion and usable audio are different boundaries; neither establishes human hearing or consent. A bounded business check may continue while the conversation gives a truthful pending response. Compare actual speech-end-to-first-rendered-audio observations with component timing, preserving failures and missing samples. Avoid adding overlapping durations or counting speculative output as an accepted operation. The model still cannot approve the exact supplier mutation. [L12]

followups.question: Where do you measure responsiveness?
followups.answer: Define the start, finish, population and clock limitations, then report distributions and failed turns. Endpointing, model first output, TTS startup and browser playout are supporting observations. A provider's first token or server-side audio callback does not by itself measure audible responsiveness.

followups.question: What if TTS succeeds but the browser is silent?
followups.answer: Inspect publication, subscription, received packets, decoding, browser audio state and playout evidence. Preserve successful generation without labeling it heard. A response may be generated while the track is muted, subscription is missing, playback is blocked or a disconnect retires the original room.

replacement.watch_for: Generation, published media, observed playout, human hearing and business commitment are separate facts.

updates.reason: Adds pipeline/realtime selection and defensible end-to-end timing while preserving P2 admission and playback scope.

replacement.title: Turn taking and durable intake
replacement.question: Why does the native adapter use manual turns?
answer: The opt-in P2/joined adapter needs durable acceptance before its dispatched generation. It disables competing default text intake and preemptive generation, uses manual turns, and retains the original caller-bound final transcript before awaiting external work. Repeated commit preserves an accepted input/operation identity; it does not promise exactly one generation or playback. The custom hook also uses StopResponse to prevent the SDK's automatic reply continuation after its own intake path.

Separate the signals when explaining alternatives. VAD estimates speech activity; streaming STT produces provisional/final text. A text turn detector uses transcript context and language, while an audio turn detector has different inputs. A realtime provider can own turn control instead. Endpointing applies the chosen mode's waiting policy: its maximum delay is not an end-to-end response deadline, and configured delays should not be blindly added together. Manual admission trades integration work and latency for an explicit boundary; LiveKit defaults are not defective. Tune against representative pauses, short commands, backchannels and transcription failures while preserving durable ordering and bounded generation observations. [L9, B01]

followups.question: Is a final transcript permission to mutate?
followups.answer: No. Recognition finality is an input observation, not investigation consent, exact quote confirmation or action commitment. Keep the original source binding through awaits, and submit a new separately authorized command when the user actually requests a business change.

followups.question: Could you enable preemptive generation later?
followups.answer: Only with an explicit speculative-output contract that preserves the original accepted identity and prevents speculative effects. Test changed transcripts, repeated commit, interruption and cancellation, then measure whether the latency gain survives actual returned-media and correctness checks.

replacement.watch_for: A final transcript, detector prediction or low endpointing delay does not establish durable acceptance.

evidence.label: Manual turn and preemptive generation settings
Separate runtime generation admission and identity

updates.reason: Explains VAD/STT/turn detection/endpointing separately and retains the pinned manual/StopResponse composition.

replacement.title: Interruption without losing truth
replacement.question: What should happen when the user barges in?
answer: A true barge-in should interrupt the intended old output promptly. Brief acknowledgments can instead be backchannels. Inspect the selected interruption strategy, VAD or adaptive signal, onset thresholds and representative labeled audio rather than treating every short utterance alike. Current interruption guidance separates identifying an interruption from recovering a false interruption. The recovery timeout follows an interruption; increasing it does not delay the initial cutoff or automatically fix onset false positives. [L10, L11]

In the pinned runtime, supported output can pause and later resume when an interruption is classified as false; verify configuration and output capability rather than promising universal resumption. Track the original response identity so a delayed interrupt for response A cannot stop response B. Business cancellation remains a separate command and policy. Cutting speech does not prove that a supplier request stopped, and a resumed answer must not create another accepted operation. Retain known results and observed output boundaries across interruption or reconnect. Evaluate intended stops, noise and backchannels with false/missed-interruption rates, stop/resume timing and user task outcomes; word count alone is not ground truth.

followups.question: Does every okay interrupt?
followups.answer: No. It may be feedback, consent to an unrelated conversational step, or part of a new request. Use representative audio and the selected detector's evidence. Exact business confirmation cannot be inferred merely from an acknowledgment or successful false-interruption recovery.

followups.question: Should barge in cancel background work?
followups.answer: Express that product decision as an explicit cancellation request with its own identity and receipt. Stop conversational output first, preserve possible external effects and later known results, and observe actual resource settlement instead of treating a cancelled waiter as stopped work.

replacement.watch_for: Onset detection, false-interruption recovery and business cancellation have different control points.

updates.reason: Adds false-interruption onset/recovery distinctions and response identity while retaining effect uncertainty.

replacement.title: Provider modes and observability
replacement.question: How do you know a session actually used the configured inference mode?
answer: Check the trusted selected mode, matching mint/readiness metadata and correlated usage/trace observations. scripted, local_real and provider_real remain distinct; process health or a UI badge establishes configuration only. Provider evidence does not qualify local_real, and the POC authorizes no silent cross-mode fallback. Returned audio and checked task outcomes are still required for the relevant media or quality claim.

Use the pinned telemetry contract rather than an imagined dictionary of all pipeline metrics. In Agents 1.8.11, the AgentSession-level metrics_collected event carries one typed metric and is deprecated for usage tracking; use session_usage_updated for usage and ChatMessage.metrics for per-turn latency. Per-plugin metric events remain distinct. Component timings, per-message latency and a session report have different availability and lifecycle boundaries. Keep numeric units, selected provider/model identifiers and missing values explicit. Correlate the original input, generation and business operation in controlled traces, while aggregate labels remain finite. A replay can produce another observation without another booking. Compare actual billable quantities under a dated tariff, including retries; session wall time alone is insufficient. Useful sanitized export, real inference and quality evaluation remain separate evidence. [L12, L13]

followups.question: Why no silent fallback?
followups.answer: Fallback can alter privacy, cost, latency and behavior while disguising which path produced the evidence. If introduced, record an explicit permitted transition and its model/plugin identities, preserve accepted business operations, and qualify actual output from the replacement path.

followups.question: Does scripted testing still matter?
followups.answer: Yes. Deterministic providers can establish replay, fault handling and useful progress. They cannot establish real recognition, stochastic quality, provider billing or returned-media performance. Keep their outcomes separate, and do not turn missing usage into a zero-cost successful inference claim.

replacement.watch_for: A configured mode, typed metric or completed report does not establish quality, hearing or action success.

updates.reason: Adds source-correct typed metric/usage/report boundaries without expanding provider qualification.

replacement.title: Latency climbed overnight
replacement.question: How would you investigate a p95 response latency regression?
answer: Freeze the metric, population and comparison window: for example, observed end-of-user-speech to first rendered agent audio in the same mode, region and load. Include timeouts and missing responses in user-impact accounting. Compare tails and sample counts; a new mix of cold jobs, long utterances or languages can move p95 without slowing every component.

Build a correlated timeline of recognition/turn decision, durable admission, model first output, tools, TTS startup and playout. Streaming stages overlap, so their durations are not an additive latency proof. Endpointing policies also differ by detector/provider mode; a maximum endpointing delay does not cap tools or network time. In this POC, inspect event-loop lag, startup slots, connection establishment, database locks and read/dispatch contention. The audit records preparation that includes result reads and playout, plus shared startup capacity. Reproduce one constrained case, then change the demonstrated bottleneck. A faster first response is a regression if it commits an unfinished turn, loses the accepted operation or increases false interruptions. Verify the intended invariant and useful result after the change. [L12, L13]

followups.question: Why not lower endpointing immediately?
followups.answer: A shorter wait can reduce delay by cutting the caller off. Identify whether the problem is endpoint detection, output recovery or another stage, and use labeled pauses, backchannels and stop commands. Preserve durable input ordering while measuring both latency and turn-quality changes.

followups.question: Is sub 500 ms guaranteed?
followups.answer: No universal target follows from this repository or the JD. State a proposed percentile, workload, mode, failure accounting and measurement boundary, then measure it. Provider TTFB or a tutorial table cannot establish a user-perceived response SLO.

replacement.watch_for: A tail-latency improvement must preserve input correctness, interruption quality and observed useful progress.

updates.reason: Adds controlled comparisons, mode-specific endpointing and quality checks to the original contention diagnosis.

replacement.title: Scale the right subsystem
replacement.question: How would you evolve this local POC for ten thousand concurrent conversations?
answer: Define ten thousand of what: connected callers, active audio, turns per second or pending durable cases. Freeze duration, speaking ratio, model mix, fan-out, payload sizes and retention. Measure bandwidth, agent-process memory/CPU, provider quotas, database admission and control/read capacity separately. Little's-law estimates can guide an experiment, but observed service-time and burst distributions must determine the actual envelope.

The POC uses one local SFU and has no production-capacity qualification. Public self-hosted guidance documents Redis-backed distributed room placement with a room hosted on one node; scaling many rooms does not imply unlimited capacity within one room. Agent servers and durable workers have separate lifetimes, bottlenecks and failure tests. Add workers only when downstream admission can absorb them, preserving bounded pending/active work, replay access and useful progress under saturation. A load generator that exchanges signaling, or even RTP, does not automatically exercise STT, tools, TTS, recording and independent business reconciliation. Retain a frozen manifest, raw observations, failures and owned cleanup at every ramp stage. No private Cloud topology or linear scaling result is inferred. [L2]

followups.question: What is the first load test?
followups.answer: Start with one representative room and turn workload, then ramp one dimension while retaining queue age, errors, actual resource use and independent results. Include admission rejection and recovery after overload; a success-only throughput number conceals the system's real operating limit.

followups.question: Why not add more workers immediately?
followups.answer: They can amplify database locks, provider throttling, startup contention or resource exhaustion. Diagnose the constrained subsystem first. Keep control and reconciliation able to progress, and stop the ramp when bounds or correctness assumptions no longer hold rather than extrapolating a local sample.

replacement.watch_for: Connected sessions, active inference, media capacity and retained business identities are different sizing dimensions.

updates.reason: Makes subsystem scaling, representative media/inference load and saturation evidence explicit without capacity claims.

replacement.title: Deploy while sessions are active
replacement.question: How should a rolling deployment stop taking work?
answer: Stop assigning new work before removing dependencies needed by admitted work. Self-hosted media drain, agent-server session drain, gateway dispatch and P1 lease recovery are different lifecycles. The documented media drain keeps existing rooms active, including participant joins, while rejecting new-room joins. Cloud agent rolling deployments have their own bounded old-session completion window; neither contract promises that arbitrary work survives forever. [L2, B03]

For a proposed canary, assign each new conversation to a recorded version/cohort at a trusted dispatch boundary and keep that assignment stable for its defined lifetime. Compare useful outcomes, errors and first rendered audio under comparable workloads, retaining prompt/model/tool versions. Define rollback and finite drain criteria before rollout. Observe actual child/task settlement before releasing ownership or deleting private state. Forced termination can leave external effects unknown, requiring original-identity reconciliation. Schema overlap needs an explicit compatibility contract, not runtime DDL. The current POC audit contains shutdown-order and budget inversions; it has no measured Cloud canary or production-safe rolling-deployment qualification. Start with those concrete findings and keep deployment ideas labeled as proposals.

followups.question: Can SIGKILL be a normal drain?
followups.answer: It may enforce a final time bound, but it is forced loss rather than graceful completion. Retain recovery obligations and possible external calls. A successor reconciles original state; rollback changes eligible future routing and cannot retract spoken audio or supplier effects.

followups.question: Can old and new schema code overlap?
followups.answer: Only under a documented compatible capability/migration contract. Validate old and new readers/writers against retained identities and formats before overlap. Runtime roles must not perform opportunistic DDL, and a healthy new process does not establish storage or media compatibility.

replacement.watch_for: Room drain, session drain, business recovery and rollback have separate owners and irreversible history.

updates.reason: Adds version-cohort canaries and bounded platform drain while preserving POC lifecycle findings and migration restrictions.

replacement.title: SLOs for a voice and work system
replacement.question: Which objectives would you define?
answer: Define separate objectives for setup, usable first audio, durable input acceptance, business completion and result disclosure. Specify the population, successful observation, time window and treatment of errors/timeouts. A quick pending reply can meet a conversational objective while the business result remains pending. Compare cold and warm paths, modes and language cohorts rather than averaging different experiences together.

Map supporting measurements to causes: event-loop lag, slot saturation, queue/pending age, lease takeovers, unknown effects, provider first output and cleanup incompleteness. Count accepted operations and committed outcomes from retained identities, not tool attempts, repeated callbacks or model statements. Attach model/prompt/tool/deployment versions to controlled diagnostic records so a canary's error and quality changes remain attributable. Keep low-cardinality aggregates separate from access-controlled identity joins and sampled content. User-impact burn and imminent capacity exhaustion should drive alert policy; a retry counter alone does not. Numeric usage and process health are supporting observations, not evidence of quality or physical delivery. The repository supplies signals and bounded local evidence; production thresholds, dashboards and redundant deployment still need measurement and qualification.

followups.question: What would you page on?
followups.answer: Page on sustained user harm or imminent exhaustion, such as accepted work exceeding its objective with growing unresolved effects. Choose windows and severity from measured behavior. Keep diagnostic component anomalies available without turning each retry or short provider spike into a separate incident.

followups.question: What if privacy limits transcripts?
followups.answer: Retain safe identifiers, timings, bounded error classes and numeric usage under explicit access and retention rules. Full transcript content need not become a metric label or universal trace attribute. Preserve enough provenance to reconcile outcomes without silently collecting more sensitive content.

replacement.watch_for: A successful exporter check is not proof of useful sanitized export or a satisfied user objective.

updates.reason: Expands SLOs with versioned experiments, authoritative outcome counting and actionable alert boundaries.

replacement.title: Tests that establish a contract
replacement.question: How would you test the hard parts rather than mirror the implementation?
answer: Write an externally observable invariant first: one original accepted identity, no stale action, a reconciled effect or explicit unknown, and useful later progress. Force the dangerous interleaving with barriers, actual lock observations or controlled process loss, then assert independent store/supplier facts. A helper-call assertion can pass while the user's guarantee fails.

Use deterministic contract fixtures for validation, real PostgreSQL for transaction/time rules, sockets for transport closure, installed artifacts for consumer boundaries and actual browser audio for media. Add a separate model-behavior layer: the pinned AgentSession.run surface supports explicit tool/output/handoff assertions, while live model wording or a semantic judge can remain stochastic and invoke a provider. Freeze scenarios, prompts/models/tools, judge rubric and judge version; compare candidates on the same representative cases and calibrate sampled judgments against human labels. A better average score cannot excuse a repeated effect or unauthorized tool action. Preserve failures, disagreements and artifacts, distinguishing a targeted rerun from a clean full lane. No model judge establishes process exit, physical hearing or production capacity. [B02]

followups.question: Can LLM evaluation replace assertions?
followups.answer: It supplements language-quality assessment, not independent execution truth. Calibrate it for the task and inspect false passes/failures. Exact identities, effect counts, eligibility and cleanup remain deterministic checks even when candidate wording varies or the mean judge score improves.

followups.question: What does a zero test runner mean?
followups.answer: It provides no passing behavioral evidence. Missing required setup, skips and timeouts remain nonpassing for the selected assertions. Record their cause honestly; replacing a failed manifest or widening a rubric merely to make the dashboard green invalidates the comparison.

replacement.watch_for: Deterministic assertions, stochastic behavior evaluation and actual media/fault evidence answer different questions.

updates.reason: Adds calibrated model evaluation and exact SDK test boundaries while retaining all original evidence-lane requirements.

replacement.title: Design the minimal public SDK
replacement.question: What should an application developer need to know to use one of these libraries?
answer: A consumer needs the domain operation, trusted scope setup, stable key/body rules, typed result, safe recovery action and close contract. Keep SQL schema details and internal polling private, but expose possible acceptance, exact confirmation and retained cleanup when those change the caller's next safe step. A generic retryable flag is misleading if a new key could repeat an external effect.

Build the smallest installed example that submits, inspects and closes under normal, conflict and unknown-ACK paths, using only declared exports/extras outside the checkout. Validate external values at runtime; type annotations alone do not authorize them. Keep Python and TypeScript lifecycles explicit rather than inventing cross-SDK parity. An optional graph or MCP adapter should invoke narrow public ports with the original operation identity and trusted scope. A graph checkpoint preserves its configured state, not automatically P1's exact confirmation, supplier receipts or effect recovery. Current LiveKit LangChain documentation describes a Python LLMAdapter over a compiled graph; that optional integration is not evidence the POC installed or qualified it. Refine names and defaults from consumer friction while retaining one durable execution owner. [B04]

followups.question: What belongs in a quickstart?
followups.answer: Include prerequisites, safe configuration, one successful call, original-identity reconciliation after ambiguous ACK and actual closure. Explain which errors are validation, rejection or unknown outcomes. Show enough operational behavior to prevent unsafe retries without turning the quickstart into an internal SQL manual.

followups.question: Would you expose a generic execute callback?
followups.answer: Only under an explicit serialization, permission and recovery contract. This POC intentionally exposes finite capabilities instead of caller-selected worker code. Adding graph/MCP composition should not introduce an independent queue or let a discovered tool schema stand in for exact mutation consent.

replacement.watch_for: An ergonomic wrapper must not hide the safe recovery path or create a second durable authority.

updates.reason: Connects SDK ergonomics to graph/MCP adapters and original-identity recovery without claiming optional integration is implemented.
